h: The Shame of Sinai Becomes the Awe of Shabbos

p: In the Tikkunim (Introduction, the passage beginning "The eighth level"):
"Bereishis — yarei boshes, fear and shame, etc.;
and one who has no shamefacedness,
in any event it is certain
that his forefathers' feet did not stand
yarei Shabbos, fear and Shabbos, etc."
It appears that his main exposition
only that by reversing the letters,
"So that His fear may be upon your faces"
brings a person to fear of sin.
to the fear of a human being,
"Know that when a person commits a sin
he says, 'May no person see me,'"
because he is ashamed before him.
So too, when a person pictures to himself
שֶׁמֶּלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
that the King of kings, HaKadosh Baruch Hu,
stands over him and sees his deeds
even though he does not see this
still, when he pictures it with faith,
שֶׁמַּאֲמִין שֶׁמֶּלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
believing that the King of kings, HaKadosh Baruch Hu,
(as is written in the Hagahah at the beginning of Orach Chaim);
and this is yarei boshes, fear and shame.
And for this there was the benefit of
"So that His fear may be upon your faces"
מַאֲמִין שֶׁמֶּלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
believes that the King of kings, HaKadosh Baruch Hu,
as if he sees it with his senses,
like the fear of a human being,
This is what is said in the Mishnah (Avos 5:20):
דְּאִם רַק יֵשׁ לוֹ בֹּשֶׁת פָּנִים
for if he only has shamefacedness,
he is already destined for Gan Eden,
since he will surely have the fear
Hashem our God and the God of our fathers,
that the Beis HaMikdash be rebuilt
and grant us our portion in Your Torah."
What connection does this have here?
that it is because it is the conclusion of Maseches Avos,
there are still further sayings after this.
Rather, the matter of this prayer
has a portion in the Torah,
"It is not written here 'the congregation of Yannai,'
And when a person merits his portion in the Torah
and Torah is the aspect of chochmah,
"Behold, the fear of Hashem, that is wisdom"
עַל יְדֵי זֶה יַשִּׂיג יִרְאַת ה׳
through this he will attain fear of Hashem,
שֶׁיִּרְאֶה שֶׁמֶּלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
that he will see that the King of kings, HaKadosh Baruch Hu,
that the Beis HaMikdash be rebuilt
there the fear was most manifest,
for as soon as a Jew entered there
for once he merely came to Yerushalayim
and all the more so in the Beis HaMikdash.
And this is "that the Beis HaMikdash be rebuilt
exists in olam, shanah, nefesh — place, time and soul;
and just as the Beis HaMikdash is in space,
corresponding to the holiness of the Mikdash.
Therefore, immediately with the entry of Shabbos,
as is expounded in the Gemara (Taanis 8b):
'And for you who fear My Name there shall shine…'"
And Rashi, of blessed memory, explained:
the awe of Shabbos is upon the am ha'aretz;
dread and fear fall upon him,
and he is afraid to lie,
and one can rely on his word.
This is what is said in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 24):
and about them it is said (Vayikra 19:30):
this is the Mikdash of yud."
It is based on what is said
this is the Shabbos of Shabbos eve,
that is, immediately with the entry of Shabbos
that there flows down upon him
to the two chambers of the heart.
And this fear from Shabbos in time
is like the fear of the Mikdash in space,
שֶׁמֶּלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
that the King of kings, HaKadosh Baruch Hu,
stands over him and sees his deeds.
And this is what is said in the Tikkunim cited above:
"Turn around boshes and you will find Shabbos"
one merits the holiness of Shabbos.
